title: fix(slack): gateway freezes during long reasoning streams when Slack streaming is off
body: Closes #196249 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the Gateway freezes during a long reasoning stream in a Slack session when Slack streaming is off. ## User Impact User impact: Slack sessions with `/reasoning stream` and no Slack preview keep the Gateway responsive however long the model reasons. Sessions that do show a Slack preview behave as before. ## Why This Change Was Made Outside `progress` mode, Slack merged each reasoning delta into the accumulated text twice, then handed the result to `pushToolProgress`. That call returns `false` immediately when the preview is inactive. Each merge reprocesses the whole accumulated text, so with no preview the Gateway did growing amounts of work per delta and threw the result away. Slack now returns before merging when `previewToolProgressEnabled` is false. The compositor builds its own check in `noteProgress` from the same inputs (`active`, account config, mode). So the change skips exactly the calls that could never be shown. The compositor's own `pushReasoningProgress` (`progress` mode) already checks before merging, and no other channel calls `mergeReasoningProgress`. Accepted edge case: when a preview is shown (`partial` or `block` with tool progress), each delta still normalizes the whole accumulated text. That path is unchanged here; making the accumulator incremental would be a separate change. ## Evidence Reported by @ptu-gh in #196249. - Observed on 2026.10.7: a Slack DM with `/reasoning stream`, streaming `off`, GLM-5.2 thinking `high`. The Gateway main thread ran at 100% CPU for about 75 minutes, with event-loop stalls growing to 24 s; SIGTERM could not complete. A CPU profile put the time under Slack `pushReasoningProgress` → `mergeReasoningProgress`. Details in the linked issue. ### Built Gateway in Docker (current main vs this PR) Setup: `pnpm build` of `main` (b21829a4c85f) and of this branch merged with that `main`, node 24.22.1 in Docker, no secrets. Slack runs in HTTP mode against a local stand-in for the Slack Web API and Events API (signed `event_callback` posts). The model is a local OpenAI-compatible stand-in that streams 1.2 MB of `reasoning_content` in 24-character deltas, then the reply `PROOF_FINAL_OK: the answer is 42.`. Each run is a Slack DM that first sends `/reasoning stream` (the Gateway answers "Reasoning stream enabled."), then the prompt. `/health` was polled every 500 ms with a 15 s timeout. Slack `streaming.mode: "off"`. | 1.2 MB reasoning, streaming `off` | main run 1 | main run 2 | PR run 1 | PR run 2 | |---|---|---|---|---| | Final reply after the model finished | 18 min 20 s | 21 min 43 s | 2 min 49 s | 6 min 19 s | | Message sent → final reply | 26 min 48 s | 27 min 48 s | 9 min 46 s | 12 min 28 s | | Gateway CPU time for the turn | 1569 s | 1652 s | 506 s | 629 s | | `/health` p95 / max | 200 ms / 2.28 s | 269 ms / 1.45 s | 47 ms / 0.72 s | 117 ms / 1.39 s | | `/health` polls over 1 s | 32 of 3086 | 7 of 3236 | 0 of 1150 | 3 of 1462 | | `/health` polls unanswered | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | Final Slack reply | `PROOF_FINAL_OK: the answer is 42.` | same | same | same | - Main-thread stall reports in the Gateway log for the Gateway that ran both long runs: main 524 (74 over 1 s), this PR 82 (7 over 1 s). Main also logged 85 "stalled session" warnings, this PR 20. - CPU profile (inspector, 20 s, about 100 s into a stream): on main `pushReasoningProgress` was 46.9% of main-thread samples (`normalizeReasoningProgressLine` 37.5%), idle 6.8%. With this PR it was 0.0%, idle 32%. - There was no full freeze on current main: `/health` always answered. What the user sees is multi-second event-loop stalls and a reply that arrives 18 to 22 minutes after the model finished. With this PR the Slack reasoning merge is gone; the cost that is left is outside Slack (shared assistant-text cleanup such as `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` and `findFinalTagMatches` shows up in both profiles) and is not changed here. - Controls, identical on both builds: a short (2 KB) reasoning stream with streaming `off` sends the same two Slack messages (the `/reasoning` acknowledgement and the final reply). With `streaming.mode: "partial"` and tool-progress preview on, the same short stream still shows reasoning in the draft (`Working` / `• consider the …`) and finishes with the same `chat.update` text. Every Slack write had the same text hash on main and on this PR. - Both builds ran side by side on a loaded host, so the absolute times are high; the comparison is between runs under the same load. - The regression test and its test-line allocation were dropped to keep test lines flat; the Docker runs above cover the path. ### Live run (real Gateway, real Slack) Setup: OpenClaw 2026.11.2 installed from npm. Its Slack `pushReasoningProgress` is identical to this PR's base, and the fixed runs used it with this PR's hunk applied. Real Slack workspace over Socket Mode, private test channel, one user. Model: local Qwen3.8 27B (reasoning variant) on a local OpenAI-compatible server, `/reasoning stream`. Prompt: a synthetic 16-clue logic puzzle with a unique solution, no tools. Measured: `/healthz` latency every 2 s, Gateway process CPU time, 30–45 s inspector CPU profiles of the main thread during reasoning. | | A: base, `off`, think ultra | B: fix, `off`, think ultra | B2: fix, `off`, think high | C: fix, `partial`, think high | |---|---|---|---|---| | Reasoning streamed | 20.7 KB | 15.7 KB | 26.4 KB | 44.5 KB | | Time to final reply | 3 min 9 s | 2 min 45 s | 4 min 54 s | 8 min 13 s | | `/healthz` median / p95 / max | 1.0 / 1.3 / 544 ms | 1.1 / 1.5 / 7.9 ms | 1.0 / 1.2 / 414 ms | 1.0 / 1.9 / 765 ms | | `pushReasoningProgress` → `merge` share of main-thread CPU | 0.2% → 0.6%, growing with the text | 0.00% (2 profiles) | 0.00% (3 profiles) | 0.10% → 1.6%, growing with the text | | Slack result | final reply delivered, correct | final reply delivered, correct | final reply delivered, correct | live reasoning preview rendered; final reply delivered | - With streaming `off`, the fix removes the reasoning merges entirely while the final reply is still delivered. - With a preview, reasoning still streams into the Slack draft (screenshot below). Its merge cost still grows with the text, the accepted edge case named above. - In run C the model exhausted its 16,384-token output budget on reasoning; the configured fallback model completed the reply in the same thread. This is model-side and unrelated to the change. - At these reasoning lengths on 2026.11.2 the wasted work is small, and isolated `/healthz` outliers occur with and without the fix. The Gateway-wide freeze in #196249 was on 2026.10.7, where the same path also ran secret redaction over the full text, during an hour-long stream.
